build.note: Yakuza 4 Remastered, Steam, 2024-07-21. expect_rva values are a cross-check only; the mod resolves everything at runtime.

anchor.name: REF_STEP_2C
anchor.comment: CMissionMacroColosseum step 0x2C handler. Calls every engine helper we need, so one unique pattern resolves all of them via ReadCall.

ADVENTURE_SURVIVE.comment: CMissionMacroAdventureSurvive - the macro behind BOTH Survival Tag rows (offline 332:6 and ranking 199:1, mission 304). Needed only so the flag reset can recognise a tag run ending; no slots are hooked.

ADVENTURE_ESCAPE.comment: CMissionMacroAdventureEscape - Extra Chase / Speed King. Slot 88 is the end-of-mission virtual whose ranking branch Sega deleted; the mod patches that SLOT (never the function - eleven vtable entries share +0xB56860). Its slots 62/63 look gutted but are shared base-class no-ops that this macro never enters.

SET_RESULT_VARIANT.comment: sub_3A46D0(screen, variant, holdFrames) - writes +0x1B8/+0x1BC, sets the draw gate +0x1C0=1, and plays the layout's type-0 'in' animation (which sets elem[0x2C] bit 0, the thing that actually makes it render). Relocation-free prefix.

LAYOUT_LOAD.comment: LoadLayout(obj, name, 0) - GENERIC and name-driven, no whitelist. This is what lets us load pjs_net_ranking even though its screen class was deleted.

NETRANK_LOADLAYOUT.comment: allocates a 0x128 layout and loads the widget's OWN layout name; we bypass it and load pjs_net_ranking instead

NETRANK_DRAW.comment: renders the stored int as %d into the panes

TEXPAR_LOAD.comment: sub_482780(name, slot, arg) - the ONLY caller-visible loader of a layout's texture archive ('<prefix><name>.par'), stashing the handle in a global slot table. LoadLayout never touches textures, so a layout can be live, animating and draw-gated open while being entirely invisible. We read the table's address out of the absolute displacement at +0x55 (not RIP-relative).

BUILD_PAGES.comment: sub_484510(layout, kind) - ONE-SHOT page builder. Returns 1 only on the call that actually builds; 0 while the csb request is still in flight. Never fall through on 0.

GET_PAGE.comment: sub_484220(layout, i) - returns NULL when layout->pages is NULL, and NEVER bounds-checks i.

SET_SUPPRESS.comment: sub_48AC40(elem, v) - elem[0xBC] = v. 0 = visible, non-zero = suppressed.
SET_SUPPRESS.pattern: 89 91 BC 00 00 00 C3 CC CC CC CC

HEAP_FREE.comment: sub_3C64D0(ptr) - the partner of the allocator, and null-safe (test rcx,rcx; je ret). NOT 0x3C6240, which lands mid-instruction and does not decode.

LAYOUT_RELEASE.comment: sub_483EB0(layout) - releases the pages through their vector-deleting destructor, which UNLINKS each element from the global render list at 0x1980D70. Without it the renderer walks freed memory.

IS_TEX_RESIDENT.comment: sub_102D750(id) -> 0/1. The gate that was discarding our panel. In sub_486920 at 0x486D79 the renderer picks the texture id from pane+0x4C, falls back to RS+0x1C, stores it in the draw command at +0x40, calls this, and on a false result jumps straight to the epilogue - AFTER sub_4889C0 has already transformed all four corners. That is why 1900x1000 sprites lit zero pixels. Pure read, one integer argument, no side effects; it rejects 0xFFFF and any id whose registry entry is null.

FLAG_GET.comment: GetFlag(flagMgr, group, bit, 1) -> int. Reads the committed bank via flagMgr->[0x990]+0xC group table. Read-only, used to LOG what is stuck.

FLAG_SET_RAW.comment: sub_BF8990(flagMgr, group, bit, value) - forces the COMMITTED bank bit. This is what the macro destructor sub_B57F40 uses; it does not touch the pending list.

FLAG_SET_EDGE.comment: sub_BF8B30(flagMgr, group, bit, value) - the EDGE-TRIGGERED setter Bob's talk script calls. Maintains a 32-entry pending list at flagMgr[0]; does NOTHING when the committed bank already holds the requested value. That no-op is the entire reason a played mode cannot be restarted.

DRAW_ELEMENT.comment: sub_48BC70(elem) - draws ONE layout element immediately. This is what CActionItem::vfunc+0x38 (sub_2FBAF0) calls directly every frame to put the dpad HUD on screen, bypassing the sorted global pass entirely. Our orphan layout has no owner and no draw node, so nothing calls it for us.

SET_PANE_HIDDEN.comment: sub_48B1B0(elem, paneId, hidden) - walks the pane tree for the u16 id at [[node+0x10]+8] and sets/clears flag bit 17 (0x20000) on that pane: +0x48B22D 'and [rax], 0xfffdffff' then +0x48B233 'shl r10d,0x11' / 'or [rax], r10d'. Bit 17 means HIDDEN - the draw gate at +0x486AB8 shifts it into state+0x34, and +0x486AE4/+0x486AF8 then skip the pane unless the force-draw bit 0x40000 is set. This is what PS3 uses at 0x69854C to pick Score vs Time (page 0, pane 0x22 = Time, 0x23 = Score).
SET_PANE_HIDDEN.note: matches the TAIL at +0x48B22D, not the prologue - five functions share that prologue (sub_48AF80/48ADE0/48AEB0/48B1B0/48B260, the same tree walk with different tails). Function start = match - 0x7D.

PANE_POS_REG.comment: sub_48AF80(elem, paneId, outBuf, 1) - registers outBuf to receive the POSITION of the pane with that id; sub_48A780 then fills it. Unlike the style registrar sub_48ADE0 this has NO flag-0x40 gate (tail at +0x48B002: and [rax],0xFFE7FFFF / shl r11d,0x14 / or / mov [rax+0x20],rbx), so it can legally read a non-text anchor pane. PS3 uses the same call (sub_197588) to find the two number anchors.
PANE_POS_REG.note: tail-anchored: five functions share this prologue byte for byte

PANE_EVAL.comment: sub_48A780(elem) - evaluates the pane tree and fills every buffer registered by sub_48AF80 / sub_48ADE0 / sub_48AEB0. TextBind calls it at +0x484926 and again at +0x484A4E.
PANE_EVAL.note: anchored inside the body - the prologue has two copies

FONT_STYLE_OPEN.comment: sub_6708E0(ctx, style) - sets ctx+0xD6C = style and, when style is nonzero, loads that style's face into font BANK 1 via sub_670520(ctx, -1, 1, 0), then tail-calls sub_670A70(ctx, 0). Pairs with FONT_STYLE_CLOSE; the loader overwrites the bank's globals without releasing, so the two must balance.
FONT_STYLE_OPEN.note: the `mov [rcx+0xD6C], edx` in the prologue makes this unique in .text

FONT_STYLE_CLOSE.comment: sub_66F200(ctx) - releases bank 1's resources and resets ctx+0xD6C to 0.
FONT_STYLE_CLOSE.note: the bare prologue occurs 4 times; the two relative calls disambiguate it

TAGHELP_DRAW.comment: CActionSurvivalTagHelp::Draw - the survival-tag Controls panel. Anchored on the two vmulss that scale the art (x512 then x1/2048), which is the only place in the image with this byte sequence.
TAGHELP_DRAW.note: matches at +0xBFBFB3, inside the function; entry = match - 0x83

SND_PLAY.comment: SndPlay(key=(bank<<16)|cue, int* outHandle /*nullable*/, flags, category) -> handle. The UI sound entry point: 1447 callers, r9d=0x12 for UI. Early-outs on a 'sound system ready' byte, hence the rip-relative cmp, which is wildcarded.

SND_STOP.comment: SndStop(handle, fadeFrames). Shares its prologue byte-for-byte with +0xCD8CA0 and +0xCD9F10, so the rip displacement of its voice-table lea is kept literal to make the match unique - it is as build-specific as expect_rva.

TALK_MATCH.comment: sub_BA7AA0 - the stage-pac talk matcher: (ctx, u16 out[4], talkBlock, p4). Walks the block's entry list in order, evaluates each entry's condition rows (op 3 = FlagGet(group,bit,value==0)), and stores the FIRST matching entry index per slot. Bob's post-mode lines live in entries AFTER the greetings, which is why DiagTalkMatch logs what the runtime view of the block is. The 16-byte prologue is relocatable; the detour resumes at +0x10.

COLO_SCENE.comment: sub_3927E0(stageMgr) - the coliseum scene-flag function (PS3 twin 0x6CAABC). For stage ST_TOUGI (0x66) it raises/lowers the STID_ST_TOUGI_SCNxxx flags that gate the stage's scene objects, chosen by mode. PC's tail (+0x393709) clears SCN033 (521:12, alias 1242 - the Ameba floor decal) unconditionally where PS3 keeps it; AmebaFloor post-detours it. The 16-byte prologue is relocatable; the detour resumes at +0x10 (cmp eax,0x61).

DLC_FLAG_BRIDGE.comment: sub_BCD251 - the surviving DLC->save-flag bridge (talk-script command 0x54). It calls IsDlcOwned(0x17..0x1A) and feeds each result to SetFlagByAlias with alias 0x648..0x64B. Those aliases are exactly the Extras unlock flags (group 332 bits 30..33), which is how we learned both the setter and the alias numbers. We anchor here because SetFlagByAlias has no unique prefix.

IS_DLC_OWNED.comment: sub_CB5970(ignored, bit) -> bool. Ignores its rcx argument and reads a fixed 64-byte ownership bitset, whose address we lift out of its own lea.

NETRANK_BIND.comment: sub_85E330 - the surviving network-ranking widget's pane binder. It is the cleanest caller of the generic layout-state helpers, so we anchor on it to reach them: is-loading, is-page-ready, and get-pane-by-index. Also yields the per-layout resource table (stride 0x70; element count at +0x18).

G_LAYOUT_RES.comment: IMPORTANT: this RVA holds a POINTER to the table, not the table. The access is `mov rax, qword ptr [rip+disp]` - a load - and boot stores a heap pointer here (0x48745F). Treating it as the array base reads unrelated static memory that happens to be zero, which is exactly the false 'empty resource entry' the first version of this diagnostic reported.

MISSION_TICK.comment: sub_B6AD7D - the mission manager's tick. It calls the macro factory and stores the result in its own +0x58, then reads it back through the global we lift here. That gives us the CURRENT mission macro whatever it is, so the watcher can report a mode that hangs even when it is a class we never patch and our own handler never runs.

LAYOUT_NAMES_READ.comment: sub_482E60 - reads the per-slot layout NAME table. Like the resource table, the RVA holds a POINTER (`mov rdi, qword ptr [rip+disp]`), so it must be dereferenced. Gives every live slot a readable name, which is what lets us compare the recap's slot against layouts that are visibly rendering.

LAYOUT_SLOT_COUNT_READ.comment: sub_487860 opens with `cmp ecx, [0x1980D20]; jae fail` - the authoritative upper bound on layout slots. Read it rather than trusting the 40 derived from table spacing.

PAGE_CTOR.comment: sub_484260(page, slot, r8d, r9d) - the page constructor, reached from BuildPages+0x133. It is the anchor for the texture-handle helpers because both of them are tiny stubs with no unique prefix of their own. It also documents the engine's own page setup: sub_489730 makes the element, sub_48A520 selects its animation sequence, sub_48AC40 suppresses it, and then - only when g_layoutRes[slot].flags bit 3 is set - it fetches a shared texture id and stamps it into the element with sub_48B9D0. That last pair is the step we were missing: without a texture handle the renderer builds our quads and then discards them at the residency gate in sub_486920.

SET_ANIM_VARIANT.comment: sub_48A520(elem, variant, flags) - selects an element's animation sequence. With flags bit 4 the variant index is used verbatim, and when the requested variant equals the current one (+0x48A562) it SKIPS the pane-tree rebuild and only resets the clock (+0x48A594) and speed (+0x48A59D). Used to replay page 9's NEW RECORD animation.

TEXT_API.comment:
sub_85DEC0 is the minigame ranking widget's draw, and it is the cleanest worked example of the engine's immediate-mode layout text API - which is what the panel's three dynamic strings need. It does exactly three things:
    sub_4848C0(page, mode, 0)          position the text cursor on a layout page
    g_textCtx[0xD7C] = 45056.0f        glyph size
    sub_670BD0(g_textCtx, "%d", value) printf into it
No font object has to be constructed: sub_4848C0 takes a PAGE RECORD, the same 0x30-byte thing GetPage returns, and reads the element from page+0x10. It has 924 callers, so it is the standard path rather than a widget quirk. This is anchored on the widget rather than on sub_4848C0 itself because that function has no distinctive prefix, and the widget's pattern is already proven.

TEX_GATE.comment: sub_486920+0x459 - the texture gate that decides whether a pane emits geometry: `mov eax,[pane+0x4C]; jne use; mov eax,[RS+0x1C]; IsTexResident; je skip_emit`. 0x83 bytes later, immediately after the emit call, sits `inc [g_quadCounter]`. That counter is the objective answer to 'did anything actually draw' - reading it around our own draw turns a visual judgement into a number in the log.
